prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Charlotte for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants in Charlotte — the right provider depends on your specific needs (how complex the case is, whether you need bone grafting or a sinus lift, sedation, insurance, budget, timeline, and whether you want a specialist to place the implant or a team approach). That said, here’s how to find the best clinician for you and what to look for:

Who to see
- For implant placement: a board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeon or a periodontist (both commonly place implants and manage bone/sinus grafts).
- For the final tooth/crown: a prosthodontist or a general dentist with extensive implant restorative experience.
- Many excellent practices use a team approach (specialist places the implant; a restorative dentist or prosthodontist makes the crown).

What to prioritize
- Relevant training and board/organization membership (AAOMS, AAP, AAID/ICOI, ABOMS, American College of Prosthodontists).
- Experience: how many implants they place annually and how many similar to your case.
- Use of modern diagnostics (CBCT 3D imaging), digital treatment planning, guided-surgery options.
- Ability to handle complications (bone grafting, sinus lifts, extractions).
- Before/after photos, patient reviews, and willingness to show recent cases or references.
- Clear explanation of timeline, costs (including grafts, temporary teeth), and warranty/guarantee.
- Sedation options if you want sedation or IV anesthesia.

How to verify and find providers
- Check Google/Yelp/Healthgrades/Zocdoc for patient reviews and ratings.
- Look up credentials on the North Carolina Dental Board and professional organizations (AAOMS, AAP, AAID).
- Ask your current dentist for a referral — they often refer to trusted local specialists.
- Book consultations with 2–3 providers to compare plans, timelines, and rapport.

If you want, I can:
- Find highly rated oral surgeons, periodontists, and prosthodontists in Charlotte near your ZIP code.
- Prepare a short list (with contact info, websites, and notes about services) so you can book consultations.

Tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and any preferences (specialist type, insurance, sedation), and I’ll pull a tailored list.
